rows.assessment: Zhang et al. 2023, PMID:36812318, PMCID:PMC9946354, Results: functional analysis of giant backbone proteins, second paragraph. Direct JATS match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. The study identified its East Lake, Wuhan isolate as Spirostomum minus using morphology, protargol staining and SSU rDNA, then established clonal cultures at 22 C. Actual Figure 1A shows extended and contracted cell bodies. The quoted treatment maintained viability; 38-to-16 seconds describes intervals between contractions, not contraction duration. Selected Results, Methods and Discussion, actual Figures 1, 6 and 9, and relevant supplement pages were inspected. Figure 9 is a mechanistic schematic. Supplementary Figure 7 shows shortening during death, which is insufficient for this trait. Abnormal-cell counts are in Supplementary Table 2, not Table S1 as cited in the RNAi Results. Rare twisted RNAi phenotypes do not establish contraction loss in every treated cell. The source's superscript exponents mean 10^(-6) to 10^(-2) M; the normalized plain-text quotation does not preserve superscript styling.

rows.assessment: Floyd et al. 2023, PMID:37307463, PMCID:PMC10288572, Results A, first paragraph, contiguous result clause. Direct JATS match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. Actual Figures 1A and 2A-B show Spirostomum body shortening and experimental trajectories separately from fitted curves. Methods used commercially sourced cultures and high-speed imaging without compressing cells; no species identity is inferred. Supplementary Figure S3 measures length along the central backbone curve, with increasing width. Supplementary Figure S6 states that repeated contractions of the same organism were not distinguished from contractions of different organisms: five traces are not five established biological replicates. Vorticella panels measure stalk contraction, not the body endpoint. Calcium-wave and energy models are not universal molecular proof. Selected experimental sections, actual Figures 1-2 and supplementary pages 3 and 5 were inspected; raw videos and the complete model were not reanalyzed.

rows.assessment: Katoh and Naitoh 1994, PMID:9317557, scientific Abstract item 3, first clause. Direct namespace-qualified Europe PMC MED abstract match and native VERIFIED. The same sentence contrasts graded cell-body shrinkage with all-or-nothing stalk coiling. Triton-extracted preparations in other abstract items are not the living-cell injection assay. Calcium-release causality is presented as an assumption, not direct molecular proof. Publisher HTML and PDF requests returned 403; full Methods, figures and strain provenance were not accessed. No species-wide example, quantitative threshold or universal trigger is inferred.

novelty.assessment: All unique lexical hits were inspected, using complete matching contexts for long generated or cached lines. Maintained hits concern cell-length measurement/division, fungal ring constriction, habituation of a contraction response, durotaxis, gravikinesis, kinetocyst discharge or axopodial shortening. Their generated pages, writers, tests and reviews preserve those scopes. No exact record, synonym or ungrounded exact graph node requiring migration was identified. The axopodial parent TODO seeks broader cellular contractility, not this body-specific phenotype, so it remains open.
novelty.other_contexts: Cached sources concern contractile injection systems, sponge/metazoan contraction, passive osmotic water loss, contractile vacuoles, taxon names or unrelated shortened intervals/chains. Dependency hits concern software contracts, generic actin descriptions or mammalian muscle. Community records concern interspecies distances or plant-root shortening. No cached mention is itself a maintained trait.
novelty.remote: Three PR924 generated pages repeat cell-length/division or dwarf-cell contexts. All 13 matching values in the compressed KG-Microbe JSON concern Haloplasma contractile taxonomy; two FOODON context values describe muscle tissue. These are not same-scope microbial body-contraction proposals. Eleven open/draft PR identities and descriptions were stable during the novelty screen.
novelty.parsing_limit: A colon in a retained cache filename exposed an inventory-parser assumption; the parser was corrected before inventory completion, and all 8001 occurrences were retained. The underlying history scan passed known-positive native multiset controls.

ontology_assessment: RDF inspection of pinned METPO (12617 triples), current upstream release (12649 triples), hash-verified editor conversion and remote templates found no contraction/myoneme/spasmoneme/shortening literal. Phenotype METPO:1000059 is active below quality METPO:1000188. Active motility 1000701 and motile 1000702 concern independent locomotion, not necessarily body shortening. Historical obsolete Motility spellings 0000006 and 000006 point to active 1000701; obsolete Motile 0000087 and 000088 point to 1000702. These are related broader historical leads, not exact matches. No retired identifier is revived; no external equivalence or ontology-pin change is proposed. Editor alone is not an absence proof.

METPO: Microbial Ecophysiological Trait and Phenotype Ontology

METPO provides terms for microbial ecophysiological traits and phenotypes: growth preferences (temperature, pH, salinity, oxygen), metabolism, and cell morphology of bacteria and archaea. Its primary purpose is to harmonize terminology across major microbial trait databases (BacDive, BactoTraits, Madin bacteria_archaea_traits, MetaTraits) for use in KG-Microbe. METPO uses OBO-style annotation patterns (IAO textual definitions, oboInOwl synonyms) and cites terms from OMP, MicrO, GO, ECOCORE, and PATO as definition sources.

matched_literals.value: A relation between a microbe and a quality of the environment from which the microbe was isolated. Microbe phenotype assertions belong on a separate edge (e.g. METPO:1000615 acidophilic via has_phenotype).

scope: Body shortening is not displacement caused only by stalk coiling, axopodial retraction, contractile-vacuole cycling, cellular injection systems, cytokinetic constriction, passive osmotic shrinkage, cell death or a static short-cell size. Habituation changes response probability and is not the response phenotype itself. No universal speed, fractional shortening, calcium concentration, ATP-independence, common protein or ecological function is required.

current_evidence.notes: Zhang et al. 2023, PMID:36812318, PMCID:PMC9946354, Results: functional analysis of giant backbone proteins, second paragraph. Direct JATS match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained.
